==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|sĭt}}, {{IPA|en|/sɪt/|a=RP,GA,AU}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-sit.ogg|a=US}}
** {{audio|en|en-au-sit.ogg|a=AU}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪt|s=1}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=to sit|:inh|enm:sitten<id:to sit>|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sed-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|sitten}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sittan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sittjan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sitjaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sed-||sit}}.

{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|fy|sitte}}, {{cog|nds|sitten}}, {{cog|nl|zitten}}, {{cog|de|sitzen}}, {{cog|sv|sitta}}, {{cog|nb|sitte}}, {{cog|nn|sitja}}, {{cog|da|sidde}}, {{cog|fo|sita}}, {{cog|is|sitja}}; and with {{cog|ga|suigh}}, {{cog|la|sedeo}}, {{cog|ru|сиде́ть}}.
{{col-bottom}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb|~s|~ting|sat,sate<l:dated,poetic>|+,~ten<l:archaic,dialectal>}}
[[Image:William Orpen Herbert Barnard John Everett.jpg|thumb|right|A [[w:William Orpen|painting]] of a man '''sitting'''. ({{sno|en|position|pos=0|etym=0}})]]

# {{sid|en|position}} {{lb|en|intransitive|copulative|of a person}} To be in a position in which the upper body is upright and supported by the [[buttocks]].
#: {{ux|en|After a long day of walking, it was good just to '''sit''' and relax.}}
#: {{ux|en|You're finishing the chowder if you '''sit''' there (motionless) all evening!}}
#* {{see more citations|en}}
# {{sid|en|move}} {{lb|en|intransitive|of a person}} To move oneself into such a position.
#: {{ux|en|I asked him to '''sit'''.}}
# {{sid|en|occupy}} {{lb|en|intransitive|of an object}} To occupy a given position.
#: {{ux|en|The dishes are still '''sitting''' on the table!}}
#: {{ux|en|The temple has '''sat''' atop that hill for centuries.}}
#: {{ux|en|Jim's pet parrot '''sat''' on his left shoulder.}}
# {{sid|en|rest}} {{lb|en|intransitive|copulative}} To remain in a state of repose; to rest; to abide; to rest in any position or condition.
#* {{RQ:KJV|Numbers|32|6|passage=And Moses said to {{...}} the children of Reuben, Shall your brothren go to war, and shall ye '''sit''' here?}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Love's Labour's Lost|IV|iii|passage=Like a demigod here '''sit''' I in the sky.}}
# {{sid|en|member}} {{lb|en|government}} To be a member of a [[deliberative]] body.
#: {{ux|en|I currently '''sit''' on a standards committee.}}
# {{sid|en|session}} {{lb|en|government|law}} Of a legislative or, especially, a judicial body such as a court, to be in [[session]].
#: {{ux|en|In what city is the circuit court '''sitting''' for this session?}}
# {{sid|en|bear}} To lie, rest, or bear; to press or weigh.
#* {{RQ:Taylor Holy Living|passage=The calamity '''sits''' heavy on us.}}
# {{sid|en|fit}} To be adjusted; to fit.
#: {{ux|en|Your new coat '''sits''' well.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 4-2|V|ii|passage=This new and gorgeous garment, majesty, / '''Sits''' not so easy on me as you think.}}
# {{sid|en|acceptable}} {{lb|en|intransitive|of an agreement or arrangement}} To be accepted or acceptable; to [[work]].
#: {{ux|en|How will this new contract '''sit''' with the workers?}}
#: {{ux|en|I don’t think it will '''sit''' well.}}
#: {{ux|en|The violence in these video games '''sits''' awkwardly with their stated aim of educating children.}}
# {{sid|en|cause}} {{lb|en|transitive|causative}} To [[cause]] to be [[seat]]ed or in a [[sitting]] [[posture]]; to [[furnish]] a [[seat]] to.
#: {{ux|en|'''Sit''' him in front of the TV and he might watch for hours.}}
# {{sid|en|accommodate}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To accommodate in seats; to [[seat]].
#: {{ux|en|The dining room table '''sits''' eight comfortably.}}
# {{sid|en|babysit}} {{lb|en|US|ambitransitive}} {{ellipsis of|en|babysit}}.
#: {{ux|en|I'm going to '''sit''' for them on Thursday.}}
#: {{ux|en|I need to find someone to '''sit''' my kids on Friday evening for four hours.}}
#* {{RQ:King Mist|passage=I saw {{...}} Mrs. Turman, who sometimes '''sat''' Billy when Steff and I went out {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Atlantic|url=https://www.theatlantic.com/family/archive/2024/03/teen-babysitters-intensive-parenting/677793/|title=Don’t Tell America the Babysitter’s Dead|date=2024-03-19|author=Faith Hill|passage='''Sitting''' was a “quintessentially American experience,” Yasemin Besen-Cassino, a Montclair State University sociologist and the author of ''The Cost of Being a Girl: Working Teens and the Origins of the Gender Wage Gap'', told me.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260526094120/https://www.theatlantic.com/family/archive/2024/03/teen-babysitters-intensive-parenting/677793/|archivedate=26 May 2026}}
# {{sid|en|exam}} {{lb|en|transitive|Australia|New Zealand|UK}} To take, to undergo or complete (an examination or test).
# {{senseid|en|eggs}} To cover and warm eggs for hatching, as a fowl; to brood; to incubate.
#* {{RQ:KJV|Jeremiah|17|11|passage=The partridge '''sitteth''' on eggs, and hatcheth them not.}}
# {{sid|en|paint}} To take a position for the purpose of having some artistic representation of oneself made, such as a picture or a bust.
#: {{ux|en|I'm '''sitting''' for a painter this evening.}}
# {{sid|en|relative position}} To have position, as at the point blown from; to hold a relative position; to have direction.
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1689|author=w:John Selden|journal=Table Talk
|passage=like a good miller that knows how to grind, which way soever the wind '''sits'''}}
#* {{RQ:Scott Guy Mannering|passage='''Sits''' the wind in that quarter?}}
# {{sid|en|endure}} {{lb|en|obsolete|transitive}} To keep one's seat when faced with (a blow, attack); to [[endure]], to [[put up with]]. {{defdate|13th–19th c.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1790|author=w:Amelia Opie|title=Dangers of Coquetry|volume=I|chapter=5
|passage=Louisa, who {{...}} had but ill born the commencement of this conversation, could '''sit''' it no longer, and hastily throwing up the sash, complained of the intense heat of the room.}}

=====Conjugation=====
{{en-conj|past=sat|stem=sitt|past2=sate|past_2sg_old2=sattest|past2_qual=dated, poetic|past_ptc2=sitten|past_ptc2_qual=archaic, dialectal}}

=====Synonyms=====
* {{sense|be in a position in which the upper body is upright and the legs are supported}} {{l|en|be seated}}
* {{sense|move oneself into such a position}} {{l|en|be seated}}, {{l|en|sit down}} {{qualifier|from a standing position}}, [[sit up]] {{qualifier|from a prone position}}, [[take a seat]]
* {{sense|of an object: occupy a given position permanently}} {{l|en|be}}, be [[found]], be [[situate]]d
* {{sense|be a member of a deliberative body}}
* {{sense|be accepted}} be [[accept]]ed, be [[welcome]]d, be [[well]] [[receive]]d
* {{sense|to accommodate in seats}} {{l|en|seat}}
